contract: Start with one preloaded, seekable TS188 or M2TS192 entity, its program and an ADTS AAC-LC, AC-3, E-AC-3 or MPEG audio PID, the target in 90 kHz ticks and the previous-frame or playback-preroll policy.

Choose the last frame with maximal source presentation time at or before the target. The reference scans the parser-enabled FFmpeg demuxer with NOFILLIN, reopens it and replays to the selected frame. It makes no stream discovery or decoder calls.

Both workers fold the requested, landing and discard times followed by every selected audio frame through EOF, including untimed frames. Each contributes presentation time, effective decode time (presentation time if DTS is absent), and all bytes. The source reader leaves an absent DTS absent.

Controls cover both policies and all codecs, multiple frames per PES, standalone untimed PES and explicit PTS and DTS. Single-layer AAC-LC LOAS controls select timestamped packets with a complete in-band LATM configuration and replay the dependent packets. Both landing selection and suffix delivery run within the measured operation.

Repeated cases start from a fresh reader, build an index during the first seek, deliver both packet suffixes through EOF, and require an indexed second seek. The reference scans and replays independently for each target.

Split cases seek across two consecutive entities cut at a carrier boundary inside a PES. The reference sees the same preloaded bytes as one logical stream and folds the same landing and complete suffix.
Layer III landing requires a zero main_data_begin back-pointer. Both workers preserve the later dependent frames in the suffix, with their original timing and bytes.
A repeated-seek case also splits the transport source inside a PES. Both seeks use the same ordered, contiguous parts.

MPEG-1 Layer I and II physical-offset controls place identical CRC-checked PAT and PMT sections immediately before each timestamped single-carrier PES. After indexing, the early backward Layer I and late forward Layer II repeats read only their physical suffix, preserving every payload and source clock. The reference independently scans and replays both complete suffixes through the same public demuxer API. Additional M2TS192 controls carry one complete Layer I or II frame per multi-carrier PES, with opaque four-byte prefixes, an early backward or late forward repeat and the same complete suffix/count/clock fold.
